sections.h2: Bath County offices and what each one does
sections.html:
A few courthouse offices in Owingsville run property tax for Bath County. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) values land and houses, the sheriff collects the bill, and the county clerk records deeds and receives bills that go delinquent. Every office uses a separate post office box, so a payment or an appeal needs to go to the right desk.

Who to call about a property tax bill
OfficeWhat it handlesPhone
Property Valuation AdministratorAssessments, exemption forms, appeal conferences(606) 674-6382
SheriffTax bills and payments(606) 674-2931
County ClerkDeeds, mortgages, liens, bills turned delinquent(606) 674-2613
County AttorneyLetters and payment plans on delinquent bills(606) 674-2454

The clerk's website also carries a page of delinquent taxes, handy for checking whether a parcel is listed.

Value is set as of January 1. In May the roll opens to the public, and that is when conferences and appeals take place. Bills go out in the fall. Under KRS 134.015, paying by November 1 earns a 2 percent discount, the printed amount stands until December 31, and after that come penalties of 5 percent for January and 10 percent once January is over. The sheriff stops collecting on April 15.

In a year when bills are late, the state may approve a different calendar with one month per stage. Bills for omitted property, or for a value raised on appeal, come due on the day they are prepared.

Book a conference with the Bath County PVA during the May inspection period. If you both agree on a figure, you're done. If not, file at the clerk's office and state the value you believe is right.

Under KRS 133.030 a three-member local board convenes at the county seat. Its first day goes to training and a review of recent comparable sales, and members may visit disputed properties. Five days is the ceiling unless the Department of Revenue permits more, and the decision arrives by certified mail.

  • Bring last year's sales of comparable homes, pictures of defects and an appraisal if you have one.
  • Ask how the PVA turned recorded sales into your number.
  • If the record misses a roof, well or septic problem, add a repair estimate.

The bill itself can't be contested, since the filing window closed months before it arrived.

Turning 65, or being totally disabled, lets a Bath County owner claim it on the home they live in. Apply to the PVA in the year you want it, with proof of age or disability attached.

KRS 132.810 gives one exemption per residential unit and counts a mobile home or manufactured house as a unit, a good fit where so many owners live in one. The figure tracks the cost of living and is revisited every two years, so ask the PVA what applies. An owner approved after paying gets a refund for the exempt portion. Report a sale or a death to the PVA, then the buyer or heir files a separate application.

sections.h2: Before you list a Bath County house
sections.html:
1. Ask the PVA for your parcel record and compare it with what you know about the house. Fix wrong details while you can.
  2. Call the sheriff for the current balance and any earlier years still open.
  3. Check the clerk's delinquent page to see whether the parcel appears.
  4. If you hold a homestead exemption, plan to tell the PVA when the sale closes.
  5. Agree with the buyer on who covers which part of the year's bill, and get the closing agent to record the split.

All four offices are in Owingsville, so one afternoon of calls usually settles where you stand. Send paperwork to the correct box, because a letter to one office does not reach the others.

Come April 15, the sheriff turns every unpaid bill over to the clerk, and it is recorded as a delinquency certificate and lien. From then on interest accrues at 1 percent per month, and the state's worked examples stack commissions of 10 percent for the clerk and 20 percent for the county attorney on top.

Letters go out, parcels are advertised, and in summer a private buyer can purchase the certificate and add charges of its own. KRS 134.015 also makes the tax a personal debt of the January 1 owner and lets the lien trail the property for 11 years. Ask the clerk for a payoff and the county attorney about a payment plan.

Bath County had 12,750 residents in 2020, and the 2025 estimate of 13,176 adds another 3.4 percent. The 2020 count found 5,445 housing units, with 10.4 percent of them vacant. Half of owner-occupied homes are worth more than $129,800, owners occupy 74.7 percent of homes, and renters pay a median $659. Median household income is $56,541. No building permits were logged for 2025.

With almost no new construction, the houses that change hands are mostly old ones. Age brings deferred repairs, and a PVA record that was never updated can misstate a house in either direction.

Cave Run Lake and the Daniel Boone National Forest take up a large share of the land, and rural lots, small farms and homes near the lake and forest make up much of the market. Interstate 64 crosses the county, and Owingsville is the seat and largest city.

sections.h2: Selling rural land, farms and forest-edge parcels
sections.html:
Many parcels here include acreage. Working farmland is taxed at agricultural value instead of market value, a rule drawn from Section 172A of the state constitution, and buyers will want to know whether your acreage keeps the classification. Ask the PVA before you list.

Look at the roof, the well and the septic system the way a buyer's inspector will. Where something needs work, a written estimate in your file helps in two places: it supports a lower assessment if the PVA's record assumes better condition than the house has, and it gives you a number to use when a buyer asks for a price cut.

Federal land owes no property tax, and much of the county lies within the Daniel Boone National Forest. On a rural tract, confirm that the boundary agrees with both the recorded deed and the PVA map. Sellers of rural land can also ask the county clerk what is recorded against a tract before they list it.

An older house with repairs pending and a bill sitting at the clerk's office can still sell. The payoff comes from the proceeds at closing, and the clerk quotes it for the month. A cash offer and a listing can be compared on what you net after repairs, back taxes and carrying costs.

faqs.q: Where do Bath County tax payments go?
faqs.a: To the Bath County Sheriff in Owingsville, at (606) 674-2931. Bills are mailed in the fall.

faqs.q: How long is the Bath County appeal window?
faqs.a: Only while the tax roll is open for inspection in May. Meet the PVA first, then file with the clerk on the next business day after the period closes.

faqs.q: How pricey is a Bath County home?
faqs.a: Half of owner-occupied homes are worth more than $129,800, and owners live in 74.7 percent of homes.

faqs.q: Does Bath County give a break to seniors?
faqs.a: Yes. An owner who is 65 or totally disabled can apply to the PVA under KRS 132.810 for the home they live in.

faqs.q: What follows once the clerk takes a Bath County bill?
faqs.a: Interest and fees are added, and the bill can be sold to a private buyer at a summer sale. Ask the clerk for a payoff and the county attorney about a payment plan.
